questions.correct_answer: How often the tool is right
questions.intro: Tools differ in ACCURACY (how often they are right), SPEED (how long you wait) and COST (money per task or month). Usually you cannot have the best of all three: the most accurate option may be slower and pricier. Decide what the task NEEDS. A live help chat needs speed. Checking medicine instructions needs accuracy above all. A big batch of simple sorting may need low cost. Set a minimum for what matters most ("at least 95% correct on my test set"), then choose the cheapest or fastest option that meets it.

sections.skill: Include hidden costs in the comparison

questions.domain: Work: measuring how well AI works
questions.prompt: Option R makes 150 errors per 1,000 tasks and Q makes 50. Each error takes 10 minutes to fix. How much more fixing time does R need per 1,000 tasks?
questions.intro: Hidden costs change the math. A cheaper, less accurate tool may cost more overall if people must fix its mistakes: if each error takes 10 minutes to correct, a few extra errors add up. A slower tool may be fine for overnight batches but not for customers waiting. Measure on your own test set, include the time people spend checking and fixing, and revisit the choice when prices or tools change.
